title: Children as Props Re-render Isolator
concept: Children Prop Reference Stability Across Parent Re-renders
problemStatement: Implement `simulateChildrenPattern(parentRenders, childElement)` that tracks how many times `childElement` is re-created when its parent container re-renders 5 times.
interviewTrap: This is one of Dan Abramov's most famous React mental models: 'Before You memo()', try moving state down or lifting content up.

details.name: Preserves identical child reference across parent renders

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: Passing an expensive component as the `children` prop `<Parent><ExpensiveTree /></Parent>` prevents `ExpensiveTree` from re-rendering when `Parent`'s state changes! Because `ExpensiveTree` is evaluated in the grandparent's render scope, its element reference is identical across `Parent` re-renders.

interviewCrossQuestions.question: How does the 'children as props' pattern prevent component re-renders without using React.memo?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: When Component A passes `` to Component B as children (``), `` is evaluated in Component A's render scope. When Component B re-renders due to its own internal state changes, Component B receives the exact same `props.children` object reference that was created by Component A. Because the element reference hasn't changed, React bails out of re-rendering `` during reconciliation!
interviewCrossQuestions.whyAsked: One of the highest-signal React interview questions; tests deep understanding of element reference stability.

howToExplain.opening: The children-as-props pattern isolates component re-renders by lifting children out of the re-rendering component's JSX scope, preserving element reference identity.
keyPoints: JSX elements are objects; child elements are created in the parent scope.
State changes in wrapper component do not recreate props.children.
React bails out of rendering children if element reference is unchanged.
Achieves zero-cost re-render isolation without React.memo.
howToExplain.closingImpression: Component composition is React's natural, built-in optimization tool that should be reached for before using useMemo or React.memo.
analogies: A picture frame: repainting the wooden frame (wrapper) does not require repainting the artwork inside (children).

commonMistakes.mistake: Creating children inline inside the wrapper component body.
commonMistakes.why: Evaluating JSX inside the wrapper recreates the element on every render, breaking the bailout.
commonMistakes.correct: Pass children as props from above.

followUpDeepDive.question: Where in React Fiber reconciler does this element bailout occur?
followUpDeepDive.answer: In `packages/react-reconciler/src/ReactFiberBeginWork.js` inside `checkScheduledUpdateOrContext()`, React checks `oldProps.children === newProps.children` and bails out via `bailoutOnAlreadyFinishedWork()`.
